# 06 Showcase exit/highlight/slide/prev in the browser demo

## Outcome

`examples/step-reveal.srn` exercises `exit`, `highlight`+`unhighlight`, and at least one `slide-*`
effect (alongside the existing `enter fade` content). `demos/step-reveal.html` has a working "Prev"
button. `demos/step-reveal.css` defines the new effect classes.

## Implementation guidance (not a hard requirement, but the recommended approach)

Scope every `transition` declaration to the effect class itself
(`.siren-enter-slide-left`, `.siren-exit-fade`, `.siren-highlight-glow`, etc.) — never to
`.siren-node`/`.siren-edge` base rules or to `.siren-pending`. This is what makes `next()`'s class
additions animate and `prev()`'s class removals (per ticket 04) snap instantly for free, with no
JS-side "disable transitions" mechanism needed. For `slide-*` effects, express the offset as a CSS
`transform: translate(...)` paired with the existing `opacity` fade, since the renderer positions
elements via absolute `x`/`y` on the `<rect>`/`<g>`, not via CSS layout — `transform` composes with
that positioning without fighting it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `examples/step-reveal.srn` is updated so its `timeline:` block includes at least one `exit`
  action, one `highlight` + matching `unhighlight` pair, and at least one `slide-*` effect (on
  `enter` or `exit`), in addition to the existing `enter fade` content.
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.html` has a "Prev" button wired to `controller.prev()`, updating the same
  status line as "Next"/"Reset".
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.css` defines `.siren-enter-slide-{left,right,top,bottom}`,
  `.siren-exit-fade`, `.siren-exit-slide-{left,right,top,bottom}`, `.siren-highlight-outline`,
  `.siren-highlight-glow` — each carrying its own `transition`/`transform`/`opacity` declarations,
  none of it on a persistent base rule.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @siren/core build` still exits 0 and the demo still loads the built bundle via
  `fetch()` (unchanged mechanism from the first slice) — this ticket only touches demo content and
  styling, not the build pipeline.

## Test seam

Manual/visual verification in a real browser, same as the first slice's demo ticket. The build
step (`pnpm --filter @siren/core build` exits 0) is mechanically checkable; the animations'
visual correctness (including that "Prev" genuinely snaps without a visible transition) is
confirmed by a human, not an automated assertion.
